correctness.rationale: Every positive semidefinite zonal kernel on S^3 has a uniformly convergent nonnegative normalized Chebyshev-U expansion. Exact Bernstein images at degrees 1-4 have nonnegative coefficients: for degree 3 the endpoint bounds on U_m(1/3) handle all m; for degree 4 the parity expansions with A=R_m(1/2), B=R_m(0) and explicit m=0,2,4,6 handle all m. For n>=5, an independently reconstructed exponential-generating-function finite-difference calculation gives the negative R_n coefficient eta_n=n!(n+1)^2(4-n)/(3 n^(n+1)(n+3)) of B_n R_{n+2}; all normalization and equality cases were checked. The standalone exact rational verifier completed 626 supplementary comparisons.

originality.rationale: The decisive new implication is positivity of ordinary affine degree-four Bernstein approximation on the three-sphere for every Schoenberg basis mode. The 2026 motivating preprint treats an angular circle operator and an affine two-sphere failure; known negative high-degree consequences and classical Schoenberg theory are explicitly not claimed new. value.rationale: The sharp full degree classification on the three-sphere identifies the first higher-sphere borderline where positivity survives despite the known two-sphere failure. It applies to every continuous positive-definite zonal covariance kernel, not selected test functions. The complete Chebyshev-mode coefficient sign and equality pattern is useful for preserving valid spherical kernels under finite degree approximation. The high-degree negative half alone would not constitute the claimed contribution.
